paragraphs: Sherry has dedicated her career to improving government systems for children and families as a senior policymaker in two presidential administrations, social entrepreneur, and public interest attorney.

Previously, she served as the head of social impact at OpenAI and led the division of the White House Office of Management and Budget charged with overseeing the development of education, labor, and social services policies and budgets. She founded and led Foster America, a nonprofit dedicated to reforming the U.S. child welfare system, and served as a domestic policy advisor to then-Vice President Biden in the Obama Administration.

Earlier in her career, she was a senior education counsel in the U.S. Senate and a children’s civil rights attorney at the Juvenile Law Center. Sherry holds a master’s in philosophy from the University of Cambridge, a master’s in public policy from Harvard, and a J.D. from Columbia.
bio.description: Sherry has dedicated her career to improving government systems for children and families as a senior policymaker in two presidential administrations, social entrepreneur, and public interest attorney.

people.name: Caitlin Mills
people.role: Co-Founder & Chief of Research and Impact

paragraphs: Caitlin is an Associate Professor in the Educational Psychology Department at the University of Minnesota. She received her Ph.D. in Cognitive Psychology from the University of Notre Dame and completed postdoctoral training in Cognitive Neuroscience at the University of British Columbia.

Her research program centers on engagement, mind-wandering, and affect during complex learning and everyday life. She has published over 100 peer-reviewed papers and was recently awarded the Tom Trabasso Young Investigator Award from the Society for Text and Discourse. She serves on multiple editorial boards and has co-chaired several conferences including Educational Data Mining and Learning Analytics and Knowledge.
bio.description: Caitlin is an Associate Professor in the Educational Psychology Department at the University of Minnesota.

paragraphs: Raquel is an engineering leader with experience ranging from startups to big tech to nonprofits to government. She has worked within the federal government to responsibly advance AI initiatives while minimizing risk and spent 9 years at Google as a software engineer on computer vision, accessibility, and social impact efforts.

Raquel holds a Ph.D. in Computer Science from MIT and a B.A. in Mathematics from Harvard. She is a founding member of Latinas in Computing and an advocate and mentor for people entering computing fields through nontraditional paths.
bio.description: Raquel is an engineering leader with experience ranging from startups to big tech to nonprofits to government.

people.name: Jenny Bradbury
people.role: Vice President of Education Innovation and Partnerships

paragraphs: Jenny leads educator recruitment and training for AugmentED’s R&D efforts, builds and manages cross-disciplinary teams, and establishes networks organized around common education goals.

Prior to joining AugmentED, she served as Senior Director of R&D for EdTech and Emerging Technologies at Digital Promise, where she brought together educators, technology developers, and researchers to co-design innovations with and for historically and systematically excluded learners. She helped develop and operationalize the Inclusive Innovation model, an R&D approach rooted in community that elevates the voices of those with greatest proximity to challenges and solutions.
Jenny has also held leadership positions at Discovery Education and the Network for Teaching Entrepreneurship, and began her career as a high school English and Humanities teacher.
bio.description: Jenny leads educator recruitment and training for AugmentED’s R&D efforts, builds and manages cross-disciplinary teams, and establishes networks organized around common education goals.

paragraphs: Abby is a software developer and technical lead, specializing in taking projects from research prototypes to deployed products in startup environments.

Previously, she has led teams as an early employee and as a co-founder at several early-stage startups, specializing in backend architecture and cloud infrastructure for robotics, IoT, and scientific AI applications.
She earned her M.S. in ECE from Georgia Tech and B.S. in EE from UCLA.
bio.description: Abby is a software developer and technical lead, specializing in taking projects from research prototypes to deployed products in startup environments.

people.name: Andrew Lan
people.role: Associate Professor of Computer Science, University of Massachusetts Amherst

paragraphs: Andrew Lan develops artificial intelligence (AI) and especially natural language processing (NLP) methods to enable scalable and effective personalized learning in education. His research covers areas such as learner modeling, personalization, content generation, and human-in-the-loop AI.
bio.description: Andrew Lan develops artificial intelligence (AI) and especially natural language processing (NLP) methods to enable scalable and effective personalized learning in education.

people.name: Ryan Baker
people.role: Professor of Artificial Intelligence and Education, Adelaide University

paragraphs: Ryan uses Educational Data Mining/Learning Analytics to understand how students interact with and learn from digital learning platforms. He develops automated detectors that assess constructs such as student engagement and behavior in real time. Ryan is also an Adjunct Professor at University of Pennsylvania’s Graduate School of Education and directs the Penn Center for Learning Analytics.
bio.description: Ryan uses Educational Data Mining/Learning Analytics to understand how students interact with and learn from digital learning platforms.

paragraphs: Angela conducts research at the intersection of learning sciences, AI, and human-computer interaction. She uses multimodal data to understand students’ cognitive and social states in collaborative STEM learning, focusing on equitable educational technologies that support student and teacher agency.
bio.description: Angela conducts research at the intersection of learning sciences, AI, and human-computer interaction.

paragraphs: Laura studies how people learn and communicate through text and discourse. She uses computational linguistics to analyze the detailed, nuanced processes of learning, and then applies these insights to design adaptive educational technologies.
bio.description: Laura studies how people learn and communicate through text and discourse.

paragraphs: Blair studies student emotional and motivational states during learning and assessment. Her research focuses on developing personalized educational systems that are sensitive to students’ experience with the educational system, personal characteristics, and the contexts in which they live and learn to promote engagement and deeper learning.
bio.description: Blair studies student emotional and motivational states during learning and assessment.

paragraphs: Isa studies how young people construct and negotiate identity across relationships and contexts, over time, and within systemic inequities. She uses qualitative methods to explore identity processes in STEM and the ways that families shape STEM identity development.
bio.description: Isa studies how young people construct and negotiate identity across relationships and contexts, over time, and within systemic inequities.

paragraphs: Neil is a startup founder, full stack engineer, and public servant who turns messy, ambiguous problems into software that meaningfully impacts people’s lives. He builds products across both Silicon Valley and the federal government.
bio.description: Neil is a startup founder, full stack engineer, and public servant who turns messy, ambiguous problems into software that meaningfully impacts people’s lives.

paragraphs: Brandon is a hands-on software engineer who turns complex technical challenges into production-ready AI/ML systems, data platforms, and secure cloud infrastructure across civic technology, enterprise, and startup environments.

Previously, he co-built a federal department’s first generative AI platform and led engineering teams delivering critical systems for immigration and humanitarian missions. He has also built feature stores and model serving pipelines to operationalize petabyte-scale data at John Deere and developed trust and safety tools to detect harmful content at Facebook.

Brandon holds a B.S. in Computer Science from Iowa State University and a J.D. from Cornell Law School. He is also a U.S. Air Force veteran who served as an Arabic linguist supporting counterterrorism operations.
bio.description: Brandon is a hands-on software engineer who turns complex technical challenges into production-ready AI/ML systems, data platforms, and secure cloud infrastructure across civic technology, enterprise, and startup environments.
